atAGlance: Cà phê trứng is Hanoi egg coffee, with strong robusta under whipped egg cream and a 1946 milk-shortage story behind the cup.
whatItIs: Cà phê trứng is Hanoi’s egg coffee, created when fresh milk was scarce and whipped egg yolk became a clever creamy cap for strong Vietnamese coffee. Expect bittersweet robusta underneath and a custardy, almost tiramisu-like top.
howToEnjoy: Use a spoon to taste the foam first, then sip through to the coffee so the bitter and custard layers meet.
howLocalsOrder: Cà phê trứng is a café treat, so choose hot if you want the egg cream thick and custardy. Ask less sweet before it is made; stirring too early flattens the creamy top.
worthKnowing: The drink is usually linked to Nguyễn Văn Giảng of Café Giảng in Hanoi, often dated to 1946. That origin story matters: it turns a moment of milk scarcity into a signature of Vietnamese café ingenuity.
goodToKnow: Contains egg and is rich enough to treat like dessert. Served hot, it shows the Hanoi origin best because the egg cream stays thick and warm.
